Window: 8:00 AM ET

Eighty-four years. That's how long Asheville, North Carolina waited for the PGA Tour to come back.

The inaugural Biltmore Championship opens Round 1 today at The Cliffs at Walnut Cove — the first PGA Tour event the city has hosted since 1942. It's the opening event of the FedExCup Fall, where players fight to secure their 2027 Tour cards. The purse is $5 million, with $900,000 going to the winner.

And the player with everything to prove is Jackson Koivun. The 21-year-old from Auburn is the tournament favorite at +1200. He's already won the 3M Open this season — becoming one of the more dynamic young players in professional golf. He's also a member of the USA Presidents Cup team, which tees off next week at Medinah. For Koivun, this week is both a warm-up and a test.

Other names to watch include Jacob Bridgeman (+1600), Ben James (+2200), and Davis Thompson (+2500). Justin Thomas withdrew Monday to rest before the Presidents Cup.

Golf Channel carries television coverage from 3–6 p.m. ET today. PGA Tour Live on ESPN+ runs featured groups starting at 7 a.m.

The history here is real. So is the field. Round 1 is live.

facebook.long_form:
Window: 10:30 AM ET

Seven days from now, the 2026 Presidents Cup begins at Medinah Country Club in Medinah, Illinois.

USA Captain Brandt Snedeker's squad is set. Automatic qualifiers: Scottie Scheffler, Cameron Young, Wyndham Clark, Russell Henley, Sam Burns, and Collin Morikawa. Captain's picks: Xander Schauffele, Justin Thomas, Patrick Cantlay, Chris Gotterup, Jacob Bridgeman, and Jackson Koivun — the 21-year-old making his Presidents Cup debut as the youngest member of the U.S. team.

International Captain Geoff Ogilvy leads a roster that includes Adam Scott, Hideki Matsuyama, Ryan Fox, and nine others representing the rest of the world outside Europe.

The United States has won 13 of 15 Presidents Cup editions — a dominance that has occasionally made the event feel one-sided. But Ogilvy's International team is built around players with genuine major pedigree, and Medinah is a course that rewards precision over power. The 2026 edition may be closer than the historical record suggests.

Koivun is the player to watch on the American side. The rookie is playing in this week's Biltmore Championship as a tune-up before Medinah — an extraordinary 10-day stretch for a 21-year-old in his first professional season.

Chapter 11 filed Sept. 8. Oct. 13 is the next court date.

The clock is ticking on "LIV 2.0." ⛳ #LIVGolf #Golf

x_posts.label: Post 3-2

LIV Golf's plan if the bankruptcy works out:

🏌️ Return in 2027
🌍 4 events: Saudi Arabia, Australia, South Africa, Hong Kong
👥 Players as majority owners
💷 BC Partners providing financing

Jon Rahm: still "noncommittal." Oct. 13 deadline in 26 days. #LIVGolf

facebook.long_form:
Window: 10:30 AM ET

LIV Golf's bankruptcy clock is ticking.

The circuit filed Chapter 11 on September 8 in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of New Jersey. Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund — which invested an estimated $6 billion in LIV since its 2022 launch — has since provided $49.6 million in debtor-in-possession financing to keep the organization operational during restructuring. London-based BC Partners is leading the effort to build what insiders are calling "LIV 2.0."

The Oct. 13 court deadline forces the next round of legal decisions. The restructuring plan envisions a return to competition in 2027 with four events — Saudi Arabia, Australia, South Africa, and Hong Kong — and a player-majority ownership structure. That structure, if it materializes, would mark a fundamental shift in how professional golf's challenger circuit operates.

The creditor list reveals where the money went. Jon Rahm is owed $7.5 million — the largest unsecured player claim. Bryson DeChambeau is owed approximately $5.8 million. Dustin Johnson, $5.5 million. These are just the unsecured claims; the total player obligations run far higher.

Rahm has publicly said he is "noncommittal" about LIV 2.0. That phrase carries enormous weight for a circuit trying to convince its biggest names to stay.

📍 Sept. 17-20: Biltmore Championship (Asheville, NC) — FAVORITE
📍 Sept. 24-27: Presidents Cup at Medinah — USA team debut

21 years old. Rookie season. Two of the biggest weeks of his life. ⛳ #PGATour #PresidentsCup

facebook.long_form:
Window: 8:30 AM ET

Jackson Koivun has a very busy 10 days ahead.

This week: he tees off in Round 1 of the Biltmore Championship in Asheville — as the tournament's favorite at +1200. It's the first event of the FedExCup Fall, and Koivun enters with a season that already includes a PGA Tour win (3M Open), an Auburn degree, and a first professional season that has exceeded almost every expectation.

Next week: he heads to Medinah Country Club for the 2026 Presidents Cup, where he'll represent the United States as the youngest member of Brandt Snedeker's team. His debut will come against the International side in matches that begin September 24.

It's a stretch that few rookies have ever faced. At 21, Koivun is simultaneously trying to win a tournament and preparing for his first major team golf event — on back-to-back weekends.

The test isn't just physical. It's mental. The best young players in professional golf learn to compartmentalize quickly. This 10-day stretch will tell us a lot about who Jackson Koivun is becoming.

stories.title: Asheville's Golf Comeback — First PGA Tour Event Since 1942

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
The last PGA Tour event in Asheville, North Carolina was in 1942.

84 years later, the inaugural Biltmore Championship opens Round 1 today.

Named for the Biltmore Estate — George Vanderbilt's 1895 mansion that put Asheville on the map.

Welcome back. ⛳ #BiltmoreChampionship

facebook.long_form:
Window: 8:00 AM ET

The last time a PGA Tour event came to Asheville, North Carolina, the year was 1942. The world was at war. The American golf circuit was months away from suspending its schedule entirely.

Eighty-four years passed. The city grew. It became a mountain destination, a cultural hub, a place known as much for its arts scene as its Blue Ridge views. In 2024, Hurricane Helene devastated the region — a flood that claimed lives and tested the city's resilience in ways it is still working through today.

And now, on September 17, 2026, the PGA Tour returns.

The Biltmore Championship takes its name from the Biltmore Estate — George Vanderbilt's 8,000-acre estate and 178,000-square-foot chateau that opened in 1895 and remains the largest privately owned home in the United States. The estate defined Asheville's identity more than any other single structure, drawing visitors from around the world and anchoring the region's economy for more than a century.

The Cliffs at Walnut Cove is the host venue. The purse is $5 million. The best golfers in the world are here.

For the golf community and for Asheville, this week is more than a tournament. It's a homecoming — 84 years in the making.

#BiltmoreChampionship #PGATour | Follow Golf Fanrecap for coverage all week.
